_what: THE REACHABILITY REGISTER. Every capability named below is one this repository DECLARES must be reached from shipping code, together with the production call site that proves it. The checker (`ProductionReachabilityRegisterTests`) recomputes each verdict from the source text and asserts the computed verdict EQUALS the declared one, in both directions.
_the_defect_this_exists_for: Brine scenarios drive INJECTED FAKES — correctly, by design, so logic can be proven without hardware. Nothing in that arrangement asserts that PRODUCTION CODE EVER CALLS THE LOGIC. Green therefore proves the code is RIGHT, not that it is REACHED. Four instances in one day: (1) `PocketBLEClient.download` shipped as a complete, unit-tested protocol client with ZERO callers under `App/`, and all eight Pocket feature files passed anyway; (2) `PocketDurableSync`, `PocketFastSyncCoordinator` and the stored-file live-boundary lifecycle were written, tested, and had zero callers, while the Pocket flow was reported delivered; (3) `StoredFileLiveBoundarySpy`'s five counters have zero write sites anywhere outside the spy itself, and the commit that added them claimed 'the counters now have real production write sites' — false on `main` and still false here; (4) in the sibling `foundry` repository a `link_provider_sub` field was added to a handler the iOS client never calls, and every test passed because the tests called the handler directly.
_why_a_register_and_not_a_heuristic: 'Every public symbol must have a caller' is unshippable noise: a library target's whole job is to publish symbols an app has not called yet, and a gate that reds on all of them is a gate people delete. This is a REGISTER — a curated table of capabilities somebody DECIDED must be reachable, each with the caller that proves it. A row that matches nothing is a failure, and a capability whose declared caller no longer calls it is a failure. Both directions, exactly like the `NounAlignmentCensus` residue rows and the P3 contract register's `served` equality: a capability that starts being reached has to MOVE this file, and one that stops being reached goes red without one.
_why_this_shape_and_not_a_third_one: Two idioms already exist and this is their intersection, not a third. The sibling `foundry` repo keeps declaration tables at `ci/registers/*.toml` with prose headers, `[[row]]` entries and residue in both directions. This repo keeps App-side construction censuses in Swift (`BrainSelectionCompositionTests` pins `CellStore(`'s construction sites to an EXACT file list; `DeviceCompositionRootGateTests` reads `App/` because `swift test` cannot compile it) and already keeps one JSON register read by repo path at `Tests/FoundryXConformanceTests/registers/p3-contract-elements.json`. JSON read by `#filePath`-relative path, checked by a Swift test in `Tests/FoundryXBrineTests/`, is the existing shape for 'a declaration table a Swift gate compares against measured reality'. The three-valued verdict is borrowed outright from that register's `met` / `unmet` / `not-reached`.
_three_verdicts_never_two: `reachable`, `unreachable`, `undetermined`. THE THIRD ONE IS THE POINT. Three false reds in one day came from a checker that could not tell 'nothing calls this' from 'I cannot see who calls this', and reported the second as the first. A text register cannot follow a protocol existential, cannot read another repository, and cannot know whether an unregistered production file is itself reached. Each of those is recorded as `undetermined` WITH THE REASON, and `undetermined` is never counted as a pass for the capability — it is counted as a question nobody has answered. Collapsing it into `unreachable` would make this gate the disease it was built to cure.
_not_satisfiable_by_a_test: A caller inside `Tests/`, `TestSupport/` or `UITests/` is not production reachability; that is the entire point. The checker enforces it structurally: `production_roots` and `non_production_roots` are disjoint and asserted disjoint, every resolved node path must be under a production root, and a `via` or `unregistered_production_file` that resolves under a non-production root is a NAMED HARD FAILURE rather than a satisfied row. `tested_from`, where a row declares it, is the opposite claim — the test files that DO exercise a capability nothing production reaches — and it is compared for EQUALITY against a scan of the non-production roots, so the contrast 'N test files, 0 production sites' is a measured number rather than a sentence.
_what_this_replaces: Ad-hoc one-off versions of this check are already scattered through the suite — `DevicePagePresentationTests` greps for `PocketOnboardingView` presenters, `UnifiedRecordingDeviceListFeatureTests` does the same check again 900 lines away, `BrainSelectionCompositionTests` pins `CellStore(`. Each was written after a specific orphan shipped. This is the place a new one goes instead of a new bespoke grep.
_mutation: Delete or rename any declared caller line and the row's computed verdict falls to `unreachable` while the register still declares `reachable` — RED, naming the capability, the file and the anchor. Add a production caller for a row declared `unreachable` — RED, demanding promotion. Point a `via` at a file under `Tests/` — RED, naming it as a test caller. Break a `declaration_anchor` — RED as a DEAD ROW. Change a `via` to `unregistered_production_file` — the verdict moves to `undetermined`, not to `unreachable`, and the counts move with it.
_mutations_run: EIGHT MUTATIONS, ALL KILLED, executed against `0c2659e` BEFORE this register was trusted — a gate nobody has watched fail is not a gate. M1: delete the only production caller of `PocketBringOver.run` in `App/DeviceScreen.swift` -> RED on THREE rows at once (`pocket-bring-over-run`, `pocket-ble-download`, `pocket-durable-sync-ordering`), because reach is transitive and a per-symbol grep could not have seen the other two. AND THE POINT OF THE WHOLE EXERCISE: under that same mutation `swift test --filter Pocket` reported `Executed 27 tests, with 0 failures` — the defect class reproduced live, with this gate the only thing that noticed. M2: rename the `SettingsScreen(` call in `App/RootView.swift` -> RED on THIRTEEN rows; one broken link near the root and everything below it falls. M3: add a production call to `StoredFileDeviceLifecycle.runFullLinkLifecycle` -> RED naming `App/DeviceScreen.swift` and demanding the row be promoted out of the red roster. M4: point `pocket-ble-download`'s caller at a file under `Tests/` -> RED twice, named as a non-production root. M5: rename `walWritten` at its own declaration -> RED as a DEAD ROW. M6: the SAME REAL CALLER as M1, merely de-registered as an `unregistered_production_file` -> computed `undetermined`, NOT `unreachable`, naming the file and the reason. That is the mutation that proves the two states are distinguished rather than merged, and it is the one a naive gate would have reported identically to M1. M7: make `link_provider_sub` appear in `App/SettingsScreen.swift` -> RED on the cross-repository row. M8: the COORDINATED edit — flip `pocket-durable-sync-import` to `reachable` AND move `verdict_counts` to agree -> STILL RED, because the verdict is recomputed from the source text and never read from this file.
_stated_limits: (1) CONTAINMENT IS FILE-LEVEL. A node is a file; a call site inside a dead function of a live file still counts as reached from that file. Function-level containment needs a parser, and a lexer that pretended to have one would be a worse lie than a stated limit. (2) The checker is a LEXER — it strips comments and blanks string literals (reusing `AppSourceTree.code(of:)`, which knows Swift's nesting block comments and multiline strings) but knows nothing of `#if`, so code behind a false `#if` counts as a call. That is the safe direction here: it over-reports reach, so it is recorded as a limit rather than relied on. (3) A capability's OWN declaring file is excluded from the undeclared-caller scan, so internal recursion is not mistaken for external reach.
_entry_points: The files whose reachability is taken as GIVEN, because they are how the process starts. Everything else must chain to one. Keeping this list to one row is deliberate: an entry point is an axiom, and a register that can add axioms freely can make anything reachable.

The command is real and the client parses its reply, but `MCU&STE&<n>` is an integer whose MEANING is unknown: pocket-libre's PROTOCOL.md names the opcode and not the enumeration, and no capture has ever correlated a value with a state of the device. Wiring it would put a number on a surface with nothing true to say about it, which is the fabricated-firmware defect (`DeviceMetricsPresentation`'s `2.4.1`) with a different field. capabilities.name: PocketBLEClient.deviceInfo — all four information reads on one session
capabilities.why: AN AGGREGATE THE SHIPPED PATH DELIBERATELY DOES NOT USE. `deviceInfo()` asks BAT, FW, SPACE and STE and returns all four as `PocketField`s. Three of those are now read individually by `PocketRecordingDeviceBridge.observe`; the fourth is `deviceState`, declared unreachable above because nobody has decoded what its integer means. So calling this would issue one extra command per session to obtain a value no surface may render — and it would do it on a client whose `protected(_:)` retires the whole session on a timeout, which is exactly the risk the bridge orders its reads to contain. Kept rather than deleted because it is the honest shape of a full information sweep the day STE is decoded; enumerated rather than silent because 'present, unreached and unenumerated' is the state this register exists to make impossible.

capabilities.name: PocketRemovalAck.read — the full-frame matcher for a four-way prefix collision
capabilities.declaration_anchor: public static func read(_ frame: String) -> PocketRemovalAnswer {
capabilities.why: `MCU&D` IS A STRICT PREFIX OF THREE OTHER FRAMES THIS SAME FIRMWARE EMITS: `MCU&D&ERR` (the refusal), `MCU&DIRS&<date>` and `MCU&DIRS_SUM&005` (a recorder merely listing the days it holds). A matcher written `hasPrefix("MCU&D")` reads all four as a successful removal, so a listing would read as five deletions and a refusal would read as a success. This splits at the protocol's own delimiter and compares the opcode FIELD whole. Registered because an unreached matcher is indistinguishable from no matcher.

capabilities.why: this line replaced `AmbientNotifier.requestAuthorizationIfNeeded()`, which raised the OS permission alert anonymously on every launch. _verdict_counts_are_equality: Declared as exact counts, never bounds. A bound would let the unreachable roster grow by one without anybody moving this file, which is precisely how four capabilities reached `main` unreached.
_floor: A register that lost its rows would be a silent full pass, so the population is asserted before its contents are.
